recent_posts.title: Issue 749 – iOS Dev Weekly
recent_posts.summary: iOS Dev Weekly issue 749 covers several topics: a new community-driven Swift Playgrounds index site called Swiftgrounds.dev, Flutter's transition from CocoaPods to Swift Package Manager as the default, tips for reducing pbxproj bloat using Xcode Groups vs Folders, a balanced take on AI coding tools, and IndustrialKit — a Swift framework for robotics control. Also highlighted is a free DMG production tool and a reflection on the cognitive value of stepping away from problems.

recent_posts.title: Issue 747 – iOS Dev Weekly
recent_posts.summary: iOS Dev Weekly issue 747 covers Swift's expanding IDE support across Cursor, VSCodium, Kiro, and Google's Antigravity via the Open VSX Registry, with commentary on VS Code's outsized influence on the editor ecosystem. Also covered: a new Metal-based Swift game engine (Untold Engine) with visionOS support, a workaround for a clipboard paste bug in Xcode 26.4 Simulator, a six-part series on Swift structured concurrency and task cancellation, a detailed guide to the macOS App Sandbox, and a deep dive into ancient date bugs in Apple SDKs.

recent_posts.title: Issue 748 – iOS Dev Weekly
recent_posts.summary: Issue 748 of iOS Dev Weekly covers several topics. The editorial focuses on the growing problem of LLM-generated pull requests overwhelming open-source maintainers, highlighting Hummingbird's new AI tool policy as a model for projects to follow. Tool highlights include a FormatStyle Guide built with Swift via WebAssembly, and Luca, a decentralized CLI tool and AI agent skills manager for teams. Code links cover Swift package traits now configurable in Xcode 26.4, a lightweight push notification service using Cloudflare Workers and Swift, and building a custom SwiftUI List replacement with ScrollView and lazy stacks. A new boutique ad network called Guild Ads is also introduced.

recent_posts.title: Issue 745 – iOS Dev Weekly
recent_posts.summary: iOS Dev Weekly issue 745 covers updates to the iOS Dev Directory (now open-sourced, with dark mode and design refresh), Apple's Hello Developer March 2026 post featuring a new 'New Docs' section, a new Network Throttler tool as an alternative to Apple's Network Link Conditioner, Steve Troughton-Smith's month-long experiments with OpenAI's Codex, a guide on building accessible iOS games, and a tutorial on implementing Passkeys using AuthenticationServices.

recent_posts.title: Issue 744 – iOS Dev Weekly
recent_posts.summary: iOS Dev Weekly issue 744 covers the overhyped trend of managers using AI agents like Claude Code to replace SaaS tools internally, arguing that good software requires discipline and vision beyond just code generation. The newsletter also highlights WendyOS (a Swift-first embedded Linux distro), Macky (an SSH app for controlling your Mac from your phone), SwiftUI foundations Q&A writeup, token usage tracking in Foundation Models, a Core Data vs SwiftData performance comparison, and automating Mac App Store screenshots.

recent_posts.title: Issue 743 – iOS Dev Weekly
recent_posts.summary: iOS Dev Weekly Issue 743 discusses the rise of AI-assisted coding tools in iOS development, particularly Xcode 26.3's implementation. The author argues that effective agent use requires detailed, unambiguous prompts and proper specification work before coding. The newsletter also covers the Swift Student Challenge 2026, SimTag (a simulator context tool), SwiftUI morphing animations, Swift concurrency tutorials, and FOSDEM talks including one questioning open source's future in the LLM era.

recent_posts.title: Issue 742 – iOS Dev Weekly
recent_posts.summary: This iOS Dev Weekly newsletter discusses Swift's cross-platform capabilities, highlighting real-world examples like Goodnotes using WebAssembly to share 100k+ lines of code across platforms and Spark email using Swift with Electron on Windows. The newsletter covers Xcode 26.3's new agentic coding support with Claude Code and Codex, plus MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration allowing any AI agent to interface with Xcode. Also featured: HealthQL, a new SQL-like interface for HealthKit data; Sketch's MCP server for design automation; and Birwaz, a browser-based tool for creating App Store screenshots with proper RTL and complex script support.

recent_posts.title: Issue 741 – iOS Dev Weekly
recent_posts.summary: Swift on Windows gets official workgroup support after years of platform availability, though flagship projects like Arc Browser have discontinued. Elementary UI emerges as a potential flagship for Swift on WebAssembly, offering a front-end framework that runs in browsers. The newsletter also covers FabBar, a custom tab bar implementation that improves on iOS's liquid glass design, guidance on migrating iOS apps from paid to freemium models, and a critique of intrusive software patterns that interrupt user workflows.

recent_posts.title: Issue 740 – iOS Dev Weekly
recent_posts.summary: iOS Dev Weekly Issue 740 features a review of Commander, a macOS native interface for Claude Code that simplifies AI-assisted coding workflows. Skip.tools announces it's now free and open source to address developer concerns about sustainability. The issue includes articles on AI coding agents, SwiftGodotBuilder for declarative game development, managing complex gestures in SwiftUI, and critiques of iOS 26's tab bar design. NSSpain 2025 conference videos are now available.

recent_posts.title: Issue 739 – iOS Dev Weekly
recent_posts.summary: This iOS development newsletter highlights Cupertino, a Model Context Protocol server that helps AI coding agents work better with Swift by providing access to Apple's documentation, Swift.org, and package information. The issue also features a PDF version of The Swift Programming Language book, tools for testing macOS apps with LLMs, a comprehensive guide to Universal Links implementation, and various resources including a SwiftUI/UIKit validation library and Paul Hudson's new book on AI integration in iOS apps.
